source_name: ALS SR — Riadni a pridružení členovia (member directory)
why_relevant: Enumerates SK leasing/asset-finance companies (bank-owned captives and independents) plus associated members (vendors, insurers, service providers) — a second actor map layer beyond the banking list.

source_name: Inštitút alternatívneho riešenia sporov SBA (Institute for ADR, SBA)
why_relevant: SBA-founded ADR body (established 1 July 2018, replacing the abolished bankový ombudsman as of 31 May 2018). Handles consumer disputes from payment services, payment-account switching and banking transactions — its caseload reporting is a leading indicator of consumer friction in payments. Listed by NBS as the SBA's dispute channel.

source_name: SBA Educa — certification/examination body of the Slovak Banking Association
why_relevant: SBA-affiliated body running statutory examinations for financial intermediaries. Exam volumes, syllabi and regulation-driven curriculum changes are an indirect read on distribution-channel size and on incoming regulatory requirements affecting banks/PSPs.

source_name: Asociácia obchodníkov s cennými papiermi (AOCP) — securities dealers association
why_relevant: Non-profit active since 1995; members are the principal SK capital-market firms licensed for investment services, bound by an AOCP Code of Ethics. Its member list (/zoznam.html) enumerates investment-services providers, many of which are bank subsidiaries — extends the actor map beyond deposit-taking.

source_name: Slovenská asociácia správcovských spoločností (SASS)
why_relevant: Asset-management association founded 1998; reported ~7 regular and ~18 associate members. Publishes fund-industry data and cooperates with AOCP and SBA — sector-level disclosure for the investment arms of SK banking groups.

source_name: Asociácia poskytovateľov spotrebiteľských úverov (APSÚ)
why_relevant: Represents the main SK consumer-credit providers since 1998; all members hold an NBS licence. Files formal comments (stanoviská/pripomienky) in legislative processes on SLOV-LEX and to NRSR — a direct, dated record of non-bank lender sector positions and of regulatory pressure on credit products.

source_name: Asociácia finančných sprostredkovateľov a finančných poradcov (AFISP)
why_relevant: Association of financial intermediation/advisory leaders — the distribution layer through which a large share of SK banking and insurance products is sold. Positions and member lists reveal distribution-channel economics and regulatory conflicts.

source_name: Slovenská asociácia poisťovní (SLASPO)
why_relevant: Insurance sector association (listed by NBS); relevant to the 'both sectors' scope through bancassurance and insurtech overlap, and its ombudsman arm publishes consumer-dispute material. Note: the NBS directory exposes the ombudsman URL rather than the main SLASPO domain, which must be confirmed separately.

source_name: Asociácia doplnkových dôchodkových spoločností (ADDS) & Asociácia dôchodkových správcovských spoločností (ADSS)
why_relevant: Pension pillar associations named by NBS; their members are largely subsidiaries of the same banking groups, and their statistics/positions track long-term savings flows competing with bank deposits.

source_name: Asociácia slovenských inkasných spoločností (ASINS)
why_relevant: Debt-collection association; its members are the counterparties buying/servicing NPL portfolios from SK banks and consumer lenders. Membership list is a pointer to the NPL-servicing actor set, invisible in bank-side directories.

source_name: Slovenská asociácia pre elektronický obchod (SAEC)
why_relevant: E-commerce association whose member list covers merchants, logistics and payment-acceptance-adjacent vendors — the acquiring/checkout demand side of SK payments. Publishes aktuality, statutes and expert-committee activity; has an EN members page.

source_name: IT Asociácia Slovenska (ITAS) — members
why_relevant: 100+ member private ICT sector association (founded 1999); membership includes the systems integrators and technology vendors serving SK banks and payments infrastructure — the vendor-side actor map that banking associations do not expose. Co-founder of Slovak.AI with STU and AmCham. EN mirror at /en/.

source_name: AmCham Slovakia (American Chamber of Commerce in the Slovak Republic)
why_relevant: Bilingual business chamber with corporate members including banks and technology firms, running policy committees and publishing position papers and event materials in English — an accessible EN-language route into SK financial-sector policy debate and a member directory pointer.

source_name: Slovenská obchodná a priemyselná komora (SOPK)
why_relevant: Statutory chamber (Act 9/1992 Zb., amended by 121/1996) with regional chambers in every regional capital; members are legal and natural persons in business, including financial institutions. Publishes positions on economic legislation and hosts sector events — a broad-economy chamber layer above the financial-sector associations.

source_name: European Banking Federation — Slovakia country page
why_relevant: SBA has been an EBF and European Payment Council member since 1996. The EBF country page carries standardised EN-language SK banking-sector figures and links, giving comparable cross-country framing and an English fallback when SBA publishes only in Slovak.

source_name: LobbyFacts / EU Transparency Register datacard — Slovenská banková asociácia
why_relevant: Mirrors the association's EU Transparency Register filing: declared lobbying budget, staff FTEs, policy files of interest and meetings — quantified, dated self-disclosure about the association's priorities that its own website does not publish.

source_name: Register účtovných závierok (registeruz.sk) — association financial statements
why_relevant: State register holding the statutory účtovné závierky and výročné správy of the associations themselves (example shown: ALS SR, IČO 30843707). Because most SK associations do not post annual reports on their own sites, this is the authoritative route to their audited financials, budgets and scale.

source_name: FinStat / Transparex company profiles for sector associations
why_relevant: Aggregator profiles for the associations as legal entities (SBA IČO 30813182; ALS SR 30843707; Slovak FinTech Association 51910497), including an 'udalosti' change feed (statutory bodies, address, filings) — a cheap change-detection layer on association governance.

source_name: SLOV-LEX pripomienkové konanie — association comments on financial legislation
why_relevant: Official legislative portal where associations (SBA, APSÚ, ALS SR, fintech bodies) file named, dated position comments on draft financial-sector laws. This is where association 'stanoviská' actually exist in full text even when the association's own site publishes nothing.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia — LinkedIn page
why_relevant: Fastest-updating public channel for SBA statements, events and commentary, often earlier than the website. Same applies to FINAS and ALS SR LinkedIn pages. Useful as a change-detection tripwire rather than a document source.
